article.name: claude-mem-lite
article.summary: claude-mem-lite is a Claude Code plugin that captures session activity through lifecycle hooks, batches related tool activity into observations, and exposes persistent memory through MCP and CLI tools. The reviewed source uses a local SQLite database with FTS5 text search. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: claude-mem-lite is an open-source Claude Code plugin combining lifecycle hooks, an MCP server, CLI tools, local persistent storage, and context injection. This review does not infer an individual maintainer identity from commit or profile metadata.

architecture.text: The shared schema initializes a local SQLite database and defines observation records with descriptive, project, branch, file, session, importance, and timestamp fields, alongside session, prompt, and activity-event records. FTS5 indexes and triggers maintain searchable text; database initialization uses WAL mode.

Claude Code lifecycle hooks filter activity and batch related operations into episodes; an MCP server and CLI expose explicit memory operations. Hook and server processes share the schema and data directory.

behavior.text: Automatic capture uses lifecycle hooks and episode batching before an observation is written. Explicit saves are also available. The shared update function accepts title, narrative, type, importance, lesson, and concepts; it scrubs strings and rebuilds derived search text in a transaction. The README describes degraded saves when model enrichment fails, a documented fallback not exercised here.

The MCP/CLI deletion path uses shared hard-delete orchestration. Official documentation describes a pre-delete database copy, so deletion from the active database does not establish erasure from backups or other copies.

Search uses FTS5/BM25 and accepts project, type, date, importance, and branch filters. Ranking combines recency, type, importance, lesson presence, noise, and citation-related factors; the current source also has AND-to-OR fallback and concept/PRF expansion when direct results are sparse. README-documented synonym processing and contextual recall are implementation claims, not measured quality.

Search can filter to a project, while the current-project value also affects ranking when no explicit project is supplied. The inspected query does not establish tenant authorization or isolation for users sharing one data directory.

metrics.evidence: FTS5 retrieval and query expansion are source-visible; no answerable or unanswerable cases were scored.
A field-patch update and supersession paths exist; no correction sequence was adjudicated.
The source exposes hard deletion and the README describes a pre-delete copy; no residual-copy probes were run.
Project filters and current-project ranking are source-visible; no cross-project or multi-user isolation workload was run.
Provenance and citation-related ranking state exist; no evidence adjudication was performed.
The source paths were inspected but not timed.
The README presents illustrative estimates; no resource measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected official documentation and code at the verified main head. It does not establish runtime correctness, retrieval quality, complete deletion across backups, tenant isolation, backup retention, or performance under load.

Project-aware ranking and filtering do not by themselves prove user or tenant isolation. Provenance tags and citation interaction counts do not establish evidence support or claim-level citation validation.
No system runtime, benchmark workload, or tests were run. README quality and cost claims were not reproduced and are not treated as measurements.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. This review did not execute claude-mem-lite, its tests, or any benchmark workload.
